# Audit — 2026-08

Read-only audit of `scheme-tokens@0.1.0` at commit `1f0c3f9`. No source files were changed.

Commands run: `pnpm build`, `npm pack`, `vitest run` (6 files / 112 tests, all passing), `publint --strict` and
`attw` against a packed tarball, plus resolution and reachability probes against the installed tarball.

---

## 0. Premise correction (read first)

Three of the six questions name APIs that do not exist in this repository and, per the project's own ADRs,
were removed on purpose before 0.1.

| Named in the request                                                    | Status                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `parseColor`                                                            | **Does not exist.** Removed in `ef6acd3` / `d11585a`.                    |
| `formatCssColor`                                                        | **Does not exist.** Removed in `ef6acd3` / `d11585a`.                    |
| `buildScheme`                                                           | **Does not exist.** Removed in `19bc9b7` (added in `29d5b94`).           |
| `createSchemeBuilder`                                                   | **Does not exist.** Same removal.                                        |
| `material3`                                                             | **Does not exist.** No `packages/material3`, no `src/sources/material3`. |
| `defineTokens`, `defineTokenGraph`, `defineTokenLayer`, `exportCssVars` | Exist. Audited below.                                                    |

The absence is enforced, not incidental:

- [src/index.ts:1-41](../src/index.ts) — the complete export list, 12 runtime values and 25 types.
- [tests/unit/package-boundary.test.ts:33-34](../tests/unit/package-boundary.test.ts) asserts
  `expect(root).not.toHaveProperty("parseColor")` and the same for `formatCssColor`.
- [tests/unit/package-boundary.test.ts:58-79](../tests/unit/package-boundary.test.ts) asserts no `material3`
  directory, import, or identifier anywhere under `src/`.
- [scripts/check-api.ts:16-29](../scripts/check-api.ts) pins the runtime export list exactly and
  [:153-165](../scripts/check-api.ts) fails the build if the bundle contains the text `material3`.
- [AGENTS.md:27](../AGENTS.md), [docs/color-policy.md](./color-policy.md),
  [docs/architecture.md:9](./architecture.md) all state that color parsing, conversion, gamut mapping,
  contrast policy and palette generation are outside the package boundary.

Questions 1 and part of 2 are therefore answered as "what the package actually does with a color-shaped
string", which is the answerable version of the question. Questions 3–6 map onto real code and are answered
directly.

---

## 1. Color model

**There is no color model.** A token value is an opaque `string` or an explicit `{ ref }` record
([src/core/graph.ts:29](../src/core/graph.ts) — `TokenExpression = string | TokenReference`). Nothing in the
package parses, normalizes, converts, or measures a color.

### What syntaxes are "accepted"

All of them, and equally. There is no syntax whitelist. The only string inspection anywhere in the pipeline is
[`isSafeCssDeclarationValue`](../src/exporters/selector-validation.ts) at
[src/exporters/selector-validation.ts:17-66](../src/exporters/selector-validation.ts), which runs **only at CSS
emission** and only asks "can this string break out of a CSS declaration?" It rejects control characters,
`/*`, `*/`, unescaped `\`, `;`, `{`, `}`, unbalanced `(`/`[`, unterminated quotes, and `!important`. It has no
notion of color, unit, or function name. `oklch(...)`, `#fff`, `red`, `var(--x, #000)`, and
`totally-not-a-color` are all equally valid.

### What the resolved object stores

No space, no components, no alpha. A compiled token is a flat mode→string map:

```ts
type CompiledToken<Mode extends string = string> = Readonly<Record<Mode, string>>;
```

([src/core/compiled-types.ts:36](../src/core/compiled-types.ts)). Everything else — visibility, origin,
per-mode dependencies, description, deprecated, extensions — lives in a sibling `metadataByToken` record
([src/core/compiled-types.ts:42-63](../src/core/compiled-types.ts)) specifically so mode names cannot collide
with metadata field names.

### Hex from OKLCH? Gamut mapping? Out-of-gamut detection?

No, no, and no. There is no color conversion code path in the repository. Verified by grep across `src/` for
`gamut`, `oklch`, `srgb`, `hex` — the only hits are literal test/doc fixture strings, never logic.

### `oklch(58% 0.22 285)` end to end

Executed against the packed tarball:

```
input : defineTokens({ "action.primary": "oklch(58% 0.22 285)" })
compiled: { "base": "oklch(58% 0.22 285)" }
css:
:root {
  --action--primary: oklch(58% 0.22 285);
}
byte-identical to input: true
```

The string arrives in the CSS unchanged, byte for byte. The only transformation in the whole pipeline is on
the _variable name_: `action.primary` → `--action--primary`, because `.` is encoded as `--`
([src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts:669-675](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts)).

### Documented call signatures

**`defineTokens`** ([src/core/graph.ts:257-290](../src/core/graph.ts))

```ts
// 1. single-mode
defineTokens<const Key, const Layers = readonly []>(
  tokens: Readonly<Record<Key, SingleTokenAuthoring<NoInfer<Key | LayerKeyOf<Layers>>>>>,

// 2. multi-mode
defineTokens<const Modes, const Key, const Layers = readonly []>(
  tokens: Readonly<Record<Key, MultiTokenAuthoring<NoInfer<Modes[number]>, ...>>>,
```

carrying `tokens` inline.

```ts
defineTokenLayer<const Key>(input: {

```

**`compileTokenGraph`** ([src/core/compile-token-graph.ts:69-75](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts))


**`material3`** — no signature to document; the symbol does not exist.

### Argument positions whose meaning changes with other arguments

Four, in descending severity.

**(a) `defineTokens` / `defineTokenGraph`: a plain object in `tokens[key]` means two different things
depending on whether `options.modes` was supplied.**
[src/core/graph.ts:484-514](../src/core/graph.ts) branches on whether the object contains any of
`value | visibility | description | deprecated | extensions`. If yes → expanded definition. If no → mode map.
So `{ light: "#fff", dark: "#000" }` is a _mode map_ in a multi-mode call and a _hard throw_ in a single-mode
call ([src/core/graph.ts:532-541](../src/core/graph.ts)). This is the single largest source of authoring
ambiguity in the API. It is guarded — mode names may not be any of the seven reserved metadata names
([src/core/graph.ts:97-104, 227](../src/core/graph.ts)) — and both branches are tested
([tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:111-155](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)), but the guard is a blocklist, not a
structural disambiguator.

**(b) `defineTokenLayer` accepts unbounded mode maps that only fail later.**
[src/core/graph.ts:334-338](../src/core/graph.ts) passes `modes: undefined, allowUnboundModeMap: true`. A
standalone layer will accept `{ foo: "x" }` as a one-mode map named `foo` with no validation at all; the
mismatch only surfaces when the layer is embedded into a graph
([src/core/graph.ts:702-760](../src/core/graph.ts)). The declared type is
`MultiTokenAuthoring<string, string>` — `Mode = string` — so TypeScript offers zero help here, unlike the
graph helpers.

**(c) `exportCssVars`: `options.scope` is _rejected_ when `options.modeSelectors.strategy === "selectors"`.**
[src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts:426-431](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts) returns
`invalid-scope` with "scope must be omitted with exact selectors." The same argument is required-ish in the
other two strategies (defaulting to `:root`) and forbidden in the third. This is a runtime-only constraint —
the `ExportCssVarsOptions` type permits the invalid combination.

**(d) `compileTokenGraph`: `options.selection` changes the _type_ of `result.value`, not just its contents.**
`"all"` widens the key union and flips `Complete` to `true` only if the input has a finite key union;
`{ keys: [...] }` narrows the union and is complete only for a literal tuple, not a runtime array
([src/core/compile-token-graph.ts:41-59](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts)). Well-tested in
[tests/types/authoring.test.ts:173-259](../tests/types/authoring.test.ts), but worth knowing that adding
`as string[]` to a selection array silently degrades every downstream lookup to optional.

## 3. Shorthand disambiguation

### Where the decision is made

Two parallel implementations, one per trust boundary:

| Boundary          | Function              | Location                                                                    |
| ----------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Trusted authoring | `normalizeExpression` | [src/core/graph.ts:582-608](../src/core/graph.ts)                           |
| Untrusted parsing | `parseExpression`     | [src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:1091-1131](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts) |

Both use the same rule, via `isReferenceInput` ([src/core/graph.ts:342-348](../src/core/graph.ts)): a value is
a reference **iff** it is a plain object with a `ref` key. `typeof input === "string"` returns the string
verbatim. There is no heuristic, no lookup against the token table, no "does this look like a color" check.

**A bare string is never a reference, unconditionally.** A string that is byte-identical to an existing token
key is still a literal — asserted at
[tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts:39-57](../tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts) (`literal: "brand.600"` compiles to the
string `"brand.600"`, with `dependenciesByMode.base === []`).

### `"red"`, `"transparent"`, `"currentColor"`

Executed against the packed tarball, with a real token named `red` in scope to force the collision:

```
red => "#ff0000"      deps: []            (the token itself)
a   => "red"          deps: []            value: "red"          → literal, NOT a ref to token `red`
b   => "#ff0000"      deps: ["red"]       value: tokenRef("red") → reference
c   => "transparent"  deps: []
d   => "currentColor" deps: []
```

CSS output:

```css
:root {
  --a: red;
  --b: #ff0000;
  --c: transparent;
  --d: currentColor;
  --red: #ff0000;
}
```

All three survive verbatim. `currentColor` keeps its capital `C` — the value is never lowercased or
normalized. Note the asymmetry that follows from
[`isTokenKey`](../src/core/identifiers.ts) at [src/core/identifiers.ts:8-15](../src/core/identifiers.ts):

- `"red"` and `"transparent"` are _syntactically valid token keys_, so `tokenRef("transparent")` is accepted
  at authoring time and fails later with `unknown-reference` if no such token exists.
- `"currentColor"` is **not** a valid token key (uppercase). Both `defineTokens({ currentColor: … })` and
  `tokenRef("currentColor")` throw `RangeError` immediately. It is only ever usable as a value.

### Is there a test for each?

**No.** Coverage is partial:

| Case                                                          | Test                                                                                                                                 | Status                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| Bare string is a literal, not a ref (`"brand.600"`)           | [tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts:39-57](../tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts)                                                                    | ✅ the general rule is covered |
| `"red"`                                                       | —                                                                                                                                    | ❌ no test                     |
| `"transparent"`                                               | —                                                                                                                                    | ❌ no test                     |
| `"currentColor"` as a _value_                                 | [docs/application-theme-coordinates.md:75](./application-theme-coordinates.md) uses it in a doc example compiled by `pnpm test:docs` | ⚠️ exercised, never asserted   |
| `"currentColor"` rejected as a _key_                          | —                                                                                                                                    | ❌ no test                     |
| Bare string colliding with a real token key in the same graph | —                                                                                                                                    | ❌ no test                     |

The last row is the meaningful gap: the existing test defines `literal: "brand.600"` alongside a token
_called_ `brand.600`, so the collision case is in fact covered for that one key. The color-keyword cases are
not, but they exercise the identical code path, so the risk is low — this is a documentation-by-test gap, not
a correctness gap.

### Where validated

| Concern                                                                                                          | Location                                                                                                                                               |

| Trusted envelope: non-empty, unique, `defaultMode ∈ modes`                                                       | `normalizeAuthoringModes` — [src/core/graph.ts:394-444](../src/core/graph.ts)                                                                          |
| Canonical order (default first, rest code-unit sorted)                                                           | [src/core/graph.ts:446-451](../src/core/graph.ts), [src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:1300-1308](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)                         |
| Per-token mode-map completeness + unknown-mode rejection                                                         | [src/core/graph.ts:527-580](../src/core/graph.ts), [src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:1025-1089](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)                         |
| Untrusted graph envelope                                                                                         | `parseModes` / `parseDefaultMode` — [src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:640-726](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)                                          |
| Untrusted compiled envelope                                                                                      | [src/core/parse-compiled-scheme.ts:143-220](../src/core/parse-compiled-scheme.ts), `canonicalizeModes` at [:651](../src/core/parse-compiled-scheme.ts) |
| JSON Schema                                                                                                      | [schemas/token-graph.v1.schema.json:18-28, 47-66, 126-135](../schemas/token-graph.v1.schema.json); compiled schema `$ref`s the same `mode` def         |

### Where consumed

| Concern                                              | Location                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Per-mode resolution loop                             | [src/core/compile-token-graph.ts:114-118](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts)                      |
| Memo key `` `${key}\0${mode}` ``                     | [src/core/compile-token-graph.ts:305-358](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts)                      |
| Per-mode dependency extraction                       | [src/core/compile-token-graph.ts:373-379](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts)                      |
| Per-mode reference + cycle validation                | [src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:1133-1214](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)                        |
| Canonical compiled serialization                     | [src/exporters/serialize-scheme.ts:89-146, 198-203](../src/exporters/serialize-scheme.ts)          |
| One CSS block per mode                               | [src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts:231-291](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts)          |
| Selector strategies (data-attribute / class / exact) | [src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts:399-511, 578-643](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts) |

### What two orthogonal axes would take

The package already has a documented answer, and it is **"don't"**:
[docs/application-theme-coordinates.md](./application-theme-coordinates.md) tells applications to keep
`PaletteId` and `ResolvedScheme` independent in their own state and flatten them to a private product of
compiler modes (`mono-light`, `mono-dark`, `vivid-light`, `vivid-dark`) only at the compiler boundary. The
flattened names are declared implementation details. [docs/roadmap.md:26](./roadmap.md) reinforces this:
"Future work should extend composition around the stable compiler rather than broaden the root package."

If you nonetheless wanted first-class axes, the blast radius is large, because a flat mode string is the
**primary key of every per-mode structure in the package**. Raw `mode`/`Mode` occurrence counts:

```
109  src/core/parse-token-graph.ts
 75  src/core/graph.ts
 64  src/core/parse-compiled-scheme.ts
 48  src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts
 33  src/core/compile-token-graph.ts
 14  src/core/compiled-types.ts
 13  src/exporters/serialize-scheme.ts
```

Only `identifiers.ts`, `json.ts`, `result.ts`, `unknown-description.ts`, and `selector-validation.ts` are
mode-free.

Per layer:

- **Parser (~110 + ~64 sites).** Largest single cost. `parseModes`/`parseDefaultMode` become
  `parseAxes`/`parseDefaultCoordinate`; every per-mode completeness check
  ([parse-token-graph.ts:1025-1089](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)) becomes a Cartesian-product
  completeness check. New issue codes needed for axis-shaped failures (`unknown-axis`, `missing-axis-value`,
  `duplicate-axis-key`), and `missing-mode-value` / `unknown-mode-value` change meaning. Every JSON Pointer
  under `/tokens/<key>/value/<mode>` gains a segment — and JSON Pointer semantics are a **versioned contract**
  ([docs/semver.md:12](./semver.md)).
- **Compiler (~33 sites).** Mechanically the cheapest: `resolveNode` already keys its memo on a composite
  `` `${key}\0${mode}` `` string ([compile-token-graph.ts:356-358](../src/core/compile-token-graph.ts)), so a
  composite coordinate key drops straight in. Reference and cycle validation are already per-mode loops and
  would become per-coordinate loops. Cost is roughly linear in the product size, not structural.
- **Serializer (~13 sites).** `canonicalModes` and the compiled `tokens` / `dependenciesByMode` projections
  become two-level. This is a **wire-format break**: `formatVersion` must go to `2`, and all three JSON
  Schemas plus `parseCompiledScheme` need a v2 branch. `serializeCompiledScheme` byte-stability is a versioned
  contract.
- **CSS exporter (~48 sites).** Conceptually the biggest _design_ change, smallest _code_ change. One block
  per mode becomes one block per coordinate. The `data-attribute` and `class` strategies currently emit a
  single generated suffix per mode
  ([export-css-variables.ts:473-505](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts)); with two axes they must emit
  compound selectors like `[data-palette="vivid"][data-scheme="dark"]` — which is exactly what the
  `strategy: "selectors"` escape hatch already lets applications write by hand today. `CssModeSelectors<Mode>`
  becomes a two-dimensional record.
- **Public types.** Eight declared surfaces are `Mode`-parameterized and all change shape:
  `TokenModeValues`, `TokenGraph.modes`, `MultiGraphOptions.modes`, `ModeOf`, `CompiledToken`,
  `CompiledTokenMetadata.dependenciesByMode`, `CompiledScheme.modes`, `CssModeSelectors.selectors`
  ([dist/index.d.ts:35, 57, 88, 108, 144, 149, 158, 207](../dist/index.d.ts)).

**Assessment:** a major version, roughly 400+ touched lines across all four layers, a `formatVersion: 2` wire
break, three schema rewrites, and new issue codes. The existing flatten-at-the-boundary pattern gets you the
same authoring outcome today at zero library cost, and its only real ergonomic penalty is that the exhaustive
mode tuple must be written out by hand. That penalty scales as the product of axis sizes, so it is tolerable
at 2×2 or 3×2 and unpleasant beyond that.

## 5. Packaging

### Manifest review

`exports` declares **five** keys, not four — root plus four subpaths
([package.json:32-41](../package.json)):

```
.                                              → { types: ./dist/index.d.ts, import: ./dist/index.js }
./schemas/token-graph.v1.schema.json           → (self)
./schemas/token-layer.v1.schema.json           → (self)
./schemas/compiled-scheme.v1.schema.json       → (self)
./package.json                                 → (self)
```

`files: ["dist", "schemas", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "LICENSE"]`, `type: "module"`,
`sideEffects: false`, `main` and `types` present as node10 fallbacks, no runtime `dependencies`.

### Do the subpaths actually resolve?

Yes — all five. Verified by installing the packed tarball into a clean ESM consumer and probing with
`import.meta.resolve` plus real `import`:

```
RESOLVE OK    scheme-tokens                                       -> node_modules/scheme-tokens/dist/index.js
RESOLVE OK    scheme-tokens/schemas/token-graph.v1.schema.json     -> .../schemas/token-graph.v1.schema.json
RESOLVE OK    scheme-tokens/schemas/token-layer.v1.schema.json     -> .../schemas/token-layer.v1.schema.json
RESOLVE OK    scheme-tokens/schemas/compiled-scheme.v1.schema.json -> .../schemas/compiled-scheme.v1.schema.json
RESOLVE OK    scheme-tokens/package.json                           -> .../package.json
RESOLVE FAIL  scheme-tokens/dist/index.js -> ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED   (correct — deep imports are sealed)

runtime exports: compileTokenGraph, defineTokenGraph, defineTokenLayer, defineTokens, exportCssVars,
                 parseCompiledScheme, parseTokenGraph, parseTokenLayer, serializeCompiledScheme,
                 serializeTokenGraph, serializeTokenLayer, tokenRef
JSON IMPORT OK  all three schemas + package.json
```

### One real finding

**`dist/index.d.ts` ends with a dangling source-map reference.**
[dist/index.d.ts:263](../dist/index.d.ts) emits `//# sourceMappingURL=index.d.ts.map`, but `index.d.ts.map`
is never produced by `tsdown` and is not in the tarball. `check-api.ts` even asserts the dist file list is
exactly `["index.d.ts", "index.js", "index.js.map"]`
([scripts/check-api.ts:103-107](../scripts/check-api.ts)), so the mismatch is baked into the release gate.
Consequence is cosmetic — editors and debuggers will make one 404/ENOENT lookup when resolving declaration
sources. Neither `publint` nor `attw` flags it. Fix is either emitting the map or disabling declaration
source maps in [tsdown.config.ts](../tsdown.config.ts). **Not fixed in this pass.**

Everything else in packaging is clean.

## 6. Test coverage gaps against `docs/architecture.md`

Suite baseline: 6 files, 112 tests, all passing.

### Declaration ordering — ⚠️ half covered

[docs/architecture.md:32](./architecture.md): _"Graph tokens compose first, followed by layers in array order;
a later definition replaces an earlier definition with the same key."_

| Half of the contract                      | Test                                                              | Status                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| layer _n_ overrides layer _n-1_           | [tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts:83-92](../tests/unit/core-v1.test.ts) | ✅ value **and** `origin` asserted |
| a layer overrides a **graph-level** token | —                                                                 | ❌ **no test**                     |

Every layer test in the suite uses `defineTokenGraph({ tokens: {}, layers: [...] })` — an empty graph token
record — or non-colliding keys. The graph-vs-layer precedence half of the sentence is unasserted. Verified
manually that the behavior is correct:

```
graph token `primary` = "#graphvalue", layer `brand` token `primary` = "#layerwins"
→ value: #layerwins | origin: {"kind":"layer","id":"brand"}
```

This is the single most valuable missing test in the suite: it is a documented, versioned semantic
([docs/semver.md:14](./semver.md)) resting on one `Map.set` overwrite at
[src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:786-790](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts), with nothing pinning it.

### Issue codes — ⚠️ 26 of 49 asserted, exhaustiveness unenforced

[docs/diagnostics.md:38, 43](./diagnostics.md): _"`Issue.code` values are contractual"_ and _"Issue-code
unions must represent every code an operation can emit."_

49 distinct codes are declared across the three public issue unions. **23 are never named in any test.** All
23 were confirmed reachable by direct probe, so these are unasserted, not dead:

```
duplicate-mode-key        invalid-css-options        invalid-mode-selectors   missing-mode-selector
empty-modes               invalid-data-attribute     invalid-reference        missing-token-value
invalid-class-prefix      invalid-default-visibility invalid-scope            no-selected-tokens
invalid-compile-options   invalid-deprecated         invalid-selection        unknown-mode-selector
invalid-description       invalid-extensions         invalid-token-definition unknown-mode-value
invalid-json-value        invalid-layer-id           invalid-visibility
```

No test enforces the exhaustiveness rule in either direction — that every declared code is reachable, or that
every emitted code appears in the declared union. [scripts/check-api.ts](../scripts/check-api.ts) only
SHA-256-hashes the normalized declaration text, which pins the _spelling_ of the unions but not their
_correspondence to the implementation_.

A direct `collector.add({ code: "…" })` with an out-of-union code would not compile — `IssueCollector<I>` is
generic over the union and the codes are string literals. The exposure is instead the **29 unchecked casts**
that launder issues across union boundaries (`as readonly TokenGraphIssue[]`, `as Result<never, …>`) — 14 in
`parse-token-graph.ts`, 9 in `parse-compiled-scheme.ts`, 4 in `export-css-variables.ts`, 2 in
`compile-token-graph.ts`. Each one re-types an issue produced by a generic helper (`readPlainRecord`,
`readArray`, `copyJsonValue`) as belonging to the target union without checking. They are all correct today,
but they are the mechanism by which a future code mismatch would reach a consumer silently, and nothing tests
across them.

Two smaller notes:

- `invalid-issue` is emitted at [src/core/json.ts:158, 177](../src/core/json.ts) but appears in no public
  union. It cannot leak: both call sites read only `.ok` and discard the issue. It sits inside
  `isJsonSafeIssue` ([src/core/json.ts:153](../src/core/json.ts)), which is **dead code** — exported from
  `json.ts`, imported nowhere, and not re-exported from [src/index.ts](../src/index.ts).
- The `missing-mode-selector` branch at
  [src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts:236-243](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts) appears
  unreachable: `parseExactSelectors` already guarantees a selector for every mode at
  [:620-629](../src/exporters/export-css-variables.ts) before `buildCssVarBlocks` runs. Defensive, but it
  means the code has two emit sites with only one reachable.

### JSON Pointer paths — ⚠️ shallow

[docs/diagnostics.md:31](./diagnostics.md) and [docs/semver.md:12](./semver.md) make pointer semantics
contractual.

| Aspect                                            | Test                                                                    | Status                               |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Top-level pointer (`/$schema`)                    | [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:207](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)     | ✅                                   |
| Indexed pointer (`/selection/keys/0`, `/1`)       | [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:244-253](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts) | ✅                                   |
| Nested token/mode pointer (`/tokens/unsafe/base`) | [tests/unit/css-safety.test.ts:89](../tests/unit/css-safety.test.ts)    | ✅                                   |
| **Pointer escaping (`~0` / `~1`)**                | —                                                                       | ❌ **no test**                       |
| Path on `unknown-reference`                       | —                                                                       | ❌ code asserted, path not           |
| Path on `reference-cycle`                         | —                                                                       | ❌ code + `cycle` asserted, path not |

`escapePointerSegment` ([src/core/json.ts:30-32](../src/core/json.ts)) and `escapeTokenPath`
([src/core/parse-token-graph.ts:1329-1331](../src/core/parse-token-graph.ts)) are duplicate implementations of
RFC 6901 escaping and neither has a test. The escaping _is_ reachable, despite valid token keys never
containing `/` or `~`, because invalid keys and unknown properties are still reported with a pointer:

```
tokens: { "a/b": … }  → path "/tokens/a~1b"   code invalid-token-key
top-level "a~b": 1    → path "/a~0b"          code unknown-property
```

Two independent escaping implementations with zero tests, guarding a versioned contract, is worth closing.

### Serialization ordering — ✅ well covered

[docs/architecture.md:46, 69](./architecture.md).

| Guarantee                                              | Test                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Token insertion order does not affect canonical bytes  | [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:356-376](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts), [tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:27-54](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts) |
| Mode-map and mode-envelope order do not affect bytes   | [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:356-376](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)                                                                                        |
| Compiled serialization is order-independent            | [tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:27-54](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts)                                                                          |
| Ordering is `localeCompare`-independent                | [tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:108-121](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts) — monkey-patches `localeCompare` to throw                              |
| Round-trip parse→serialize stability (all 3 artifacts) | [tests/schemas/schemas.test.ts:398-436](../tests/schemas/schemas.test.ts)                                                                                      |
| Selector-map insertion order does not affect CSS       | [tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:56-80](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts)                                                                          |
| Selected-key emission is code-unit ordered             | [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:226-254](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)                                                                                        |

No gaps found. This is the best-covered contract in the package.

### Also strong (not asked, worth recording)

- Parsers never throw for arbitrary JSON — property test, 200 runs
  ([tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:16-25](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts)).
- Input ownership / defensive copying — asserted for all three parsers and both trusted helpers by mutating
  the caller's object after the call
  ([tests/schemas/schemas.test.ts:438-554](../tests/schemas/schemas.test.ts),
  [tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:89-97](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)).
- Stack safety — 10 001-deep reference chain
  ([tests/properties/determinism.test.ts:123-142](../tests/properties/determinism.test.ts)) and a 6 000-node
  cycle bounded to 3 s ([tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts:256-267](../tests/unit/api-reset.test.ts)).

## Summary of findings

| #   | Finding                                                                                                | Severity      |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------- |
| 1   | Layer-overrides-graph-token precedence is documented, versioned, and untested                          | Medium        |
| 2   | 23 of 49 contractual issue codes have no assertion; exhaustiveness rule unenforced in either direction | Medium        |
| 3   | JSON Pointer escaping has two duplicate implementations and zero tests                                 | Medium        |
| 4   | `defineTokenLayer` accepts unvalidated unbounded mode maps typed as `Mode = string`                    | Low–Medium    |
| 5   | `dist/index.d.ts` references a `.d.ts.map` that is never emitted or shipped                            | Low           |
| 6   | `exportCssVars` rejects `scope` + exact `selectors` only at runtime; the type permits it               | Low           |
| 7   | `isJsonSafeIssue` is dead code; its `invalid-issue` code is absent from every public union             | Low           |
| 8   | `missing-mode-selector` has an apparently unreachable second emit site                                 | Informational |

Packaging, serialization determinism, parser safety, and input ownership are clean. Report only — no fixes
applied.
